issues.title: docs(workshop-2): pdoom1's Phase 1 sealed position -- coordination#47, sealed 10:18 AEST
issues.body:
pdoom1's Phase 1 sealed position for Workshop 2 (`coordination#47`, the weekend
deployment postmortem, chaired by `pdoom-data`).

**Sealed 2026-08-09 ~10:18 AEST**, before the 11:00 deadline. The seal comment is
[coordination#47 comment 5228569183](https://github.com/PipFoweraker/coordination/issues/47#issuecomment-5228569183)
and carries the repo, the commit SHA and the file's sha256 only -- not the content.

**This PR must not change the sealed SHA.** The seal points at `cec51d7e`. Merge it
as-is; if a hook rewrites the file, the seal is broken and the correct response is to
post a corrected hash on `#47` and minute it, not to quietly re-hash.

## Why the file is committed at seal time rather than at release

Last workshop the recorder held only a hash and was sole custodian, so pdoom1 could
not verify its own commitment. The recorder conceded the sharper form -- *"a commitment
you cannot cleanly re-hash is not a commitment."* `#47` ruled the fix: commit the
artefact, publish the SHA, let every seat re-hash independently.

## What is in it

- **C1** -- 20 rows, tag-to-publish, every row fetchable via `git cat-file`, `gh pr view`,
  `gh release view` or `gh run view`. **No deploy rows**: that is `pdoom1-website`'s
  evidence and guessing at it is what the instrument exists to catch.
- **C2** -- `coordination#44`'s fact-expiry class is real and covers three of eleven
  failures better than this repo's own taxonomy does. Its **single-generator claim does
  not survive**: six of seven mechanism instances have no moment at which they were true,
  and the cycle's highest-cost defect sits outside the class entirely.
  **Includes a correction of pdoom1's own published account**: per `#1184`, the old
  ladder gate DID warn over `#1137`'s range via `godot/data/`. The mechanism was
  `|| true`, not the allowlist gap. The allowlist gap is real and independently fatal
  (`d7b47a1a`, `#1101`). The tag object `v0.14.0` carries the wrong reason permanently
  and cannot be edited.
- **C3** -- one mechanism that existed and was disarmed; one composite no mechanism
  would have caught; one guard that ran daily, green, against a decoy file. Plus `#1070`:
  a correct, precise diagnosis, seven days old, that made no difference.
- **C4** -- five wins with their limits stated, including the release commit that reported
  its own 1212-green as *not evidence about this change*.
- **C5** -- **no guard counts as installed until a red run of it is recorded.** Three
  forced red runs this week. Predicted cost 2-3 agent-hours, zero Pip attention, no
  game-code change. Falsifier dated 2026-08-16.
- **Section 6** lists this seat's own errors, two of them marked **UNEVIDENCED** rather
  than dropped or dressed.

## Scope

One new file. No code, no workflow, no version file, no tag. Does not touch
`check_ladder_bump.py`, `quality-checks.yml`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `run_godot_tests.py` or
the freshness workflow -- four concurrent lanes own those.

Refs `coordination#47`, #1184, #1178

issues.title: docs(release): a league cutover playbook built from the two measured cutovers -- and the one number that blocks a public schedule
issues.body:
Commissioned by Pip, 2026-08-09:

> "we also want to start accommodating our predictable build, uplift and
> deployment times into any public facing league scheduling announcement. Can we
> get things properly queued up and then do a relatively hard and fast cutover,
> from a player's perspective"

Adds `docs/design/LEAGUE_CUTOVER_PLAYBOOK.md`. **Changes no workflow, no version
file, no tag.** Documentation only.

## The answer to the question, up front

**Not yet, and the document says exactly which piece is missing.**

| Phase | v0.14.0 | v0.14.1 | Predictable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Release PR open -> merged | 53m 08s | 9m 20s | No -- human review dominates; CI floor is 6-9 min of `Godot Tests` |
| **Tag -> release published** | **5m 18s** | **5m 28s** | **YES.** Two samples ten seconds apart, full cross-platform build included (2m47s in CI) |
| Publish -> pdoom1.com correct | 1h 10m 58s | 18m 00s | **No, and worse than "no"** -- BOTH required a human hand-dispatching website workflows |
| Publish -> pdoom1.com, unattended | never observed | never observed | **UNMEASURED** |

The "~6h45m worst case" everyone quotes -- including me, until I checked -- is
arithmetic on cron periods (`pdoom1#1182`), not an observation. **The unattended
path has never once been observed carrying a release to the live site.** That is
the single thing blocking a public schedule, and it is why the document refuses
to state a player-visible window as a time.

Whole-incident arc, for scale: v0.14.0 published 12:52:51Z -> v0.14.1 live on
pdoom1.com 16:26:24Z = **3h 33m 33s**. The release-cut lane itself was
**1h 38m 24s** (14:48:00Z -> 16:26:24Z; firm end, soft start -- the lane's start
instant is not machine-recorded and the document says so).

## What the document contains

1. **Measured timeline**, phase by phase, both cutovers, with the per-job
   breakdown of the release workflow (run `31195680192`).
2. **Eight pre-stageable items vs six that must happen at cutover.** Minimum
   player-visible switch, if the site step were solved: tag push + 5m30s.
3. **The player-visible window stated honestly**, with the derivation of the
   unattended estimate shown component by component, and what would have to
   change (four named conditions, three of which are `pdoom1-website`'s).
4. **Ladder/epoch handling** -- five facts the announcement must convey about
   what happens to existing scores, and the failure it prevents (pdoom1.com
   presenting a closed 6-entry L3 board as live while play landed on L4).
5. **Abort criteria** -- hard abort, abort-the-announcement-not-the-release,
   stop-and-fix, and explicitly what is NOT an abort.

## Four things it establishes that were not on the record

**The v0.14.0 tag was written at the wrong commit, and the record of that was
nowhere.** The first `v0.14.0` tag object `64588f82` pointed at `237636d1` --
`art(l3): fire the hero wave` on `art/l2-picks-bridge-1158`, **not an ancestor of
main**. Deleted 61 seconds later; the only machine record is the repo activity
log (`64588f82 -> 00000000` at 12:46:54Z). Its message asserted that commit was
*"the commit the verified artifact is built from"*; that sentence was **removed
rather than corrected** in the recreated tag. Resolved here: the published
artifact came from `7368e237` (run `31179700780` `head_sha`).

**The guard that was right could not have stopped it.** `pre-release-checks.yml`
correctly failed on the wrong tag at `Check version in project.godot`. It is a
**separate workflow** from `enhanced-release.yml`, which nothing makes wait for
it -- and that run went on to complete a **full cross-platform build on the wrong
tree**, dying only at `Generate Release Feeds & Metadata`. The publish was
blocked by a downstream feed job, not by the guard. (Flagged as owed work; not
fixed here, per the brief.)

**The playtest ran after publish, and the numbers are tight.** First
playtest-derived defect filed at publish +27m28s (#1171); Pip's 147-turn score on
the server at +28m54s. **Five defects as first counted (`coordination#40`), six
in the tag message, seven finally fixed** (#1179's `> Press ENTER for
Leaderboard` was 436px below the bottom of its own box). An epoch cut whose whole
point was a new board shipped with the board unreachable.

**Three docs map `v0.14 -> L3`, including `RELEASE_CALENDAR.html`, which #1152
does not name.** A public league calendar derived from any of them prints the
wrong epoch number.

## Relationship to existing docs

Extends `docs/RELEASE_AND_LEAGUE_CYCLE.html` section 5 (the L1 -> L2 epoch-cut
runbook) rather than duplicating it, adding the four things that runbook has no
step for: **tag SHA verification, live-site freshness verification, a playtest
gate before publish, and measured durations.**

## Honesty markers, since this document exists to be quoted

- Every duration traces to a run ID, git object, or GitHub API timestamp.
- The unattended-window figure is marked **ESTIMATE** with its derivation shown.
- Playtest duration is marked **UNMEASURED** and not estimated; the document
  names the three timestamps that would fix that on the next cut.
- The "eight hours" stale-site assertion is marked **UNVERIFIED** -- its only
  record is the body of PR #1182 itself.
- The 1h38m lane figure is labelled a reconstruction, not a stopwatch reading.

## Cross-repo

Coordination issue filed to `pdoom1-website` proposing the timing contract in
section 5 -- what pdoom1 will tell them and when, and what they can safely say
before it is true. Their copy and their pages remain entirely their call; this
does not design either. References `coordination#40`, `pdoom1-website#285` and
`#289`.

## Scope discipline

Stayed out of `check_ladder_bump.py`, `quality-checks.yml`, `CHANGELOG.md`,
`scripts/run_godot_tests.py` and the freshness workflow -- four concurrent lanes
own `#1178`, `#1165`, `#1181` and the `force_alarm` work.

Documentation-only; the fast gate is unaffected by this change.

issues.title: fix(changelog): stop the changelog announcing open issues as shipped (#1165)
issues.body:
Closes #1165. CHANGELOG.md is not an internal file. `sync-game-version.yml` slices a version section out of it and publishes that text to pdoom1-website as release notes, so a wrong line reaches players with no human in between. The v0.13.2 body told players #500 was delivered while #500 was open. ## 1. Ground truth, measured not assumed Every number cited in CHANGELOG.md was checked against the GitHub API (`gh api repos/PipFoweraker/pdoom1/issues/N`), not against memory or against what a commit message claimed. **142 numbers cited. 123 closed. 19 open. 0 nonexistent.** 19 of those citations sat in SHIPPED sections. That is the defect: | number | kind | state | cited in shipped section | title | |---|---|---|---|---| | #186 | issue | **OPEN** | [v0.11.0] | (0.2) Enhancement - public opinion and media system | | #500 | issue | **OPEN** | [0.12.0] | Research Quality System (Rushed/Standard/Thorough) | | #791 | issue | **OPEN** | [0.13.2] | Early economy: force a small early lease spend; bedroom/basement start hard-caps hires | | #793 | issue | **OPEN** | [0.14.0] | Office floor: all staff render as the same character + sprites oversized vs the room | | #798 | issue | **OPEN** | [0.14.0] | Put 'Buy Compute' under an operations-style submenu (action grouping) | | #802 | issue | **OPEN** | [0.14.0] | In-game music controller (mute/skip/next) + more track variety | | #811 | issue | **OPEN** | [0.13.2] | Workshop 3 (mechanics) -- Mon 07-27 / Tue 07-28 build / Wed 07-29 | | #957 | issue | **OPEN** | [0.14.0] | feat(leaderboard): optional Operator name + visually highlight own lab row | | #1063 | issue | **OPEN** | [0.14.0] | Let the player set player name + lab name on the FIRST screen | | #1067 | issue | **OPEN** | [0.14.0] | Release builds ship a STALE build_stamp.txt -- CI never runs write_build_stamp.py | | #1068 | issue | **OPEN** | [0.14.0] | The site's Linux download button 404s (PDoom.x86_64 is not a release asset) | | #1072 | issue | **OPEN** | [0.14.0] | build_release.py hardcodes the output name PDoom.exe regardless of --preset | | #1093 | issue | **OPEN** | [0.14.0] | art(review): generation was paid for and the outputs were never reviewed | | #1111 | issue | **OPEN** | [0.14.0] | Pip's rulings on the event-promotion pack, 2026-08-04 11:17 | | #1115 | issue | **OPEN** | [0.14.0] | No working re-sync path from pdoom-data | | #1117 | issue | **OPEN** | [0.14.0] | Dead-path sweep leftovers: the tests/ Python suite CI pretends to run | | #1125 | issue | **OPEN** | [0.14.0] | GO: retime first, promotions ruled, F4-F7 deferred | | #1126 | issue | **OPEN** | [0.14.0] | The Local/Global toggle silently un-presses itself on fetch failure | | #1165 | issue | **OPEN** | (this issue, cited as provenance only) | CHANGELOG.md can announce open issues as shipped | The issue predicted #500 and #483/#527. The measurement found #500 open, #483 and #527 closed -- so **the specific claim in the issue was 1-for-3, and the underlying problem was 19x worse than the issue described**. #1165's Mechanism A (the stray 2025 block inside `[0.13.2]`) had already been repaired on 2026-08-08 in `7368e237`; that part needed nothing. Mechanism B was untouched and is fixed here. The full 142-row table, generated by `python scripts/check_changelog_claims.py --report`, is at the bottom of this description. ## 2. What was actually wrong, and how it is corrected **Each of the 19 has a real merged commit behind it.** I checked (`git log --grep`): #802 has `5731dd2e`, #1068/#1072 have `129545ea`, #791/#811 have `9abe20a7`, #186 has `2b554b26` ("Phase 1"), and so on. The work is real. What was false is the implied "and therefore this issue is done". The changelog cited an issue number as if it were a receipt. **Squash-merge in this repo does NOT fire closes-keywords** (documented in CLAUDE.md), so the routine outcome is: PR merges, issue stays open, changelog claims the issue. That is most of how the gap opened, and it is why nothing here closes those issues automatically. Corrected in place, not erased. The 19 citations now read `#802 [open]`: ``` - **Pick the music from the pause menu** (#802 [open], #1146) -- track selection while you play, not only in Settings. ``` That tells a reader the release advanced an issue that is not finished, and it keeps the evidence trail. Deleting the entries would have hidden both the work and the error. The five historical `## [Unreleased]` headings (lines 589, 667, 928, 1295, 1465) are relabelled `[Unversioned]` with a dated note; **their body text is unchanged**. The one at line 7 stays. Any tool taking "the newest section" now gets exactly one answer. A `## Conventions (machine-checked)` block at the top of CHANGELOG.md documents the rules and carries the dated correction note, so the next person editing the file learns the constraint from the file itself. ## 3. The guard, and the evidence it fails `scripts/check_changelog_claims.py` (pre-commit hook `changelog-claims-check` + a CI step in `quality-checks.yml`). Same anti-rot shape as `scripts/generate_dq_index.py`: a generated artefact plus a check that blocks stale commits. Rules: - exactly one `[Unreleased]`, and it must be the first section - modern version headings dated `YYYY-MM-DD`, newest first - no released section cites an open number without an `[open]` marker - **no `[open]` marker on a number that has since closed** -- checked in both directions, so the annotation cannot rot into decoration The pre-0.9 pygame-era archive is exempt from the heading-shape rules only. It has duplicate `[0.7.4]` headings, a `[Previous]` label and out-of-order dates; rewriting an archive to satisfy a linter destroys the record it exists to keep. The `[Unreleased]` rule and the claim rule apply to the whole file. ### It fails on the file as it stood (before the corrections) ``` CHANGELOG claim check FAILED: [FAIL] CHANGELOG.md has 6 '## [Unreleased]' headings (line 7, line 589, line 667, line 928, line 1295, line 1465); exactly one is allowed. Any tool that greps for the newest section can splice unrelated years together. [FAIL] line 80: section '[0.14.0]' is a SHIPPED section but cites #802, which is still OPEN (issue: In-game music controller (mute/skip/next) + more track variety; expose the doom-triggered rotation). A released section citing an open number announces work that did not land. Either correct the entry, or write `#802 [open]` if the release genuinely advanced an issue that is not finished. ... 18 more claim failures, one per citation listed in section 1 ... [FAIL] line 234: section '[0.12.0]' is a SHIPPED section but cites #500, which is still OPEN (issue: Research Quality System (Rushed/Standard/Thorough)). ... EXIT=1 ``` ### It passes on the file as corrected ``` CHANGELOG claim check OK -- 47 sections, 142 numbers verified against changelog_issue_state.json (refreshed 2026-08-09). 18 citation(s) carry the `[open]` marker and were confirmed still open: #186, #500, #791, #793, #798, #802, #811, #957, #1063, #1067, #1068, #1072, #1093, #1111, #1115, #1117, #1125, #1126 ``` ### And it fails on a stale marker, which is the failure mode of the fix itself Injected `#1161 [open]` on a closed PR, in a scratch copy: ``` [FAIL] line 112: #1161 carries the `[open]` marker but is CLOSED (pr: feat(credits): a credits screen the cat people can actually reach). Drop the marker -- a stale 'still open' warning is its own false claim. EXIT=1 ``` ## 4. Offline / no-gh behaviour (the part worth arguing about) Ground truth is cached in `scripts/changelog_issue_state.json`, **committed**. The pre-commit hook reads that file; the normal path makes **zero network calls** and needs no `gh` auth. Only `--refresh` touches the network. When it cannot verify, it **fails** -- it does not skip, warn, or pass: ``` $ python scripts/check_changelog_claims.py # new citation, no network [FAIL] 1 citation(s) could NOT be verified (absent from changelog_issue_state.json): #1165 (line 113, section '[0.14.0]'). Run `python scripts/check_changelog_claims.py --refresh` while online, then commit the manifest. This check refuses to pass on unverified claims -- passing-when-unsure is the bug it exists to catch. EXIT=1 $ python scripts/check_changelog_claims.py # manifest deleted entirely [FAIL] 169 citation(s) could NOT be verified (changelog_issue_state.json does not exist): #1179 (line 57, section '[0.14.1]'); ... and 159 more. ... EXIT=1 ``` Justification: a skip-with-warning would recreate the exact failure class this PR exists to close -- a check that reports success while having verified nothing is what #640 (CI green on zero tests) and this issue both are. The cost is that someone genuinely offline, adding a citation to a brand-new issue, is blocked until they can run `--refresh`. That is one command and it is the rare case; every existing citation verifies offline. CI does one thing more: after the offline check it re-fetches live state and re-runs the check, so a claim that went false *after* the manifest was written is caught here rather than on the website. It fails only on a substantive violation, never on manifest churn -- a gate that goes red for cosmetic reasons gets switched off within a week (that lesson is already written into `.pre-commit-config.yaml` under #1117). ## 5. Not done here, deliberately **None of the 19 open issues were closed.** Several look finished from their commits. Deciding that from a commit message is the guess that produced the original defect, so it goes to a human. Candidates that look most likely already-done-but-never-closed: #1067, #1068, #1072, #957, #1063. Note also, since it is directly relevant to how this drifted: **squash-merge in this repo does not fire closes-keywords**, so merging this PR will NOT close #1165. Close it manually. The issue's ask 3 -- correcting the live v0.13.2 release body via `gh release edit` -- is not done here. This PR changes the repo; the published release body is a separate artefact and editing live player-facing text is a call for Pip. Worth noting the pressure is lower than when the issue was written: v0.14.1 is current, so v0.13.2's body is no longer the front page. ## Full ground-truth table (142 numbers)

issues.title: ci(release): a force_alarm drill for the freshness check, whose alarm had never once fired
issues.body:
## What was untested

PR #1182 (`1ddb033d`) added a check that curls `pdoom1.com/data/version.json` and
compares it against the latest release. Its **comparison** was proven red before
shipping -- same live site, same real response, only the expected version
changed. Its **alarm** -- the issue creation and de-duplication in the `alert`
job -- had never executed once.

Those are different halves and nothing in the Actions list distinguishes them.
An attempt to observe the alarm by dispatching with `tolerance_minutes: 0`
completed green and filed nothing, because tolerance governs how long the site
may LAG and the site is not lagging (serves v0.14.1, release is v0.14.1). Zero
tolerance against a synced site still passes. That dispatch only re-proved the
happy path.

## What this does

Adds a `force_alarm` workflow input, default `false`. It substitutes **one**
value -- the tag the site is expected to be serving -- for
`v0.0.0-FORCE-ALARM-DRILL`, and drops tolerance to zero.

Everything downstream is the production path: the same live cache-busted GET
against pdoom1.com, the same comparison in `check_site_release_freshness.py`
(file unmodified), the same exit 1, the same `if: failure()` gate, the same
issue search, the same create-or-comment. There is no mock branch. A drill that
runs a mock alert step proves the mock works.

A drill leaves a **RED** run on purpose. Red is how the alarm reaches anyone, so
a drill that stayed green would be exercising a different path.

If pdoom1.com is unreachable during a drill the script still returns 2 (UNKNOWN)
and the run stays green with no issue filed -- correct behaviour inherited from
the real path, but it means **a green `force_alarm` run is a FAILED drill**. The
step summary says so inside the run.

## De-duplication -- the part most likely to be got wrong

The alert de-dups by listing open issues labelled `release` and matching an
**exact title**. A drill filing under the real title would be a landmine: the
next genuine outage would find that open issue and take the **comment** branch,
appending a real alarm to a thread titled `[DRILL]` whose body says nothing is
wrong. Nobody triages a new comment on a drill ticket at 3am. The drill would
have disarmed the alarm it exists to prove.

So the **title is the discriminator, and it is the only thing that varies**.
Drill and real use two titles that cannot collide, and both run the same
`listForRepo` search, the same exact-title match, and the same create-or-comment
branches.

The drill deliberately **keeps** the `release` label, so it stays inside the
result set the real path reads and the exact-title discrimination is genuinely
tested rather than trivially avoided by filtering the drill out. It drops
`pdoom-website` and `priority:high` so it does not page website triage.

The `resolve` job matches the real title only. It therefore never closes a drill
issue -- a drill closed by the next scheduled run two hours later would be gone
before the operator read it -- and an open drill issue never blocks it closing a
real one.

## Evidence: the drill was actually run, twice

**Run 1** (`force_alarm: true`) --
https://github.com/PipFoweraker/pdoom1/actions/runs/31281144601 -- conclusion
`failure`, which is the intended result.

```
live site advertises : v0.14.1
latest release is    : v0.0.0-FORCE-ALARM-DRILL
release age          : 1804 min
tolerance            : 0 min
verdict=stale  pdoom1.com has advertised v0.14.1 for 1804 min after v0.0.0-FORCE-ALARM-DRILL was published
script exit code: 1
```

Alert job:

```
Open issues labelled 'release': 0. Matching on exact title: "[DRILL] alarm-path exercise -- live site release freshness (not an outage)"
Filed #1188: https://github.com/PipFoweraker/pdoom1/issues/1188
```

That is the first time this workflow's issue-creation code has ever executed.

**Run 2**, dispatched with #1188 still open --
https://github.com/PipFoweraker/pdoom1/actions/runs/31281199510 -- also
`failure`:

```
Open issues labelled 'release': 1. Matching on exact title: "[DRILL] alarm-path exercise -- live site release freshness (not an outage)"
Commented on existing #1188 (de-dup branch).
```

De-duplication took the comment branch instead of filing a duplicate. Both
branches of the alert are now evidenced.

**Non-suppression, checked against live state while #1188 was open** -- the same
search the real path runs, with the real title:

```
$ gh api "repos/PipFoweraker/pdoom1/issues?state=open&labels=release&per_page=100" \
    --jq 'map(select(.title == "pdoom1.com is serving a stale release")) | length'
0
```

Zero matches, so a genuine alarm with the drill issue open takes the CREATE
branch and files a real issue. The drill cannot silence it.

#1188 was closed after the evidence was taken.

## Runsheet

`docs/rituals/gate_6_board_opens.md`, "After the gate": dispatch with
`force_alarm` once per release cycle, confirm the `[DRILL]` issue appears, close
it. It states plainly that **a drill that has never been run is the same as a
guard that has never failed.**

## Not touched

`version.txt`, `ladder_version.txt`, no tags. Nothing in `check_ladder_bump.py`,
`quality-checks.yml`, `CHANGELOG.md` or `scripts/run_godot_tests.py` (concurrent
lanes #1178, #1165, #1181).

issues.title: ci(ladder): arm the board-key guard -- drop '|| true', add a written ack (#1178)
issues.body:
Closes #1178.

## The neutered invocation, confirmed

`.github/workflows/quality-checks.yml:79` (on `origin/main` at `1ddb033d`):

```yaml
python tools/check_ladder_bump.py --base "origin/$BASE_REF" || true
```

It was disarmed **twice**, not once. `|| true` swallows a non-zero exit, and
`tools/check_ladder_bump.py` *also* returns 0 on a warning by default
(`--strict` was never passed). Either alone would have made the step green.

## Before: proof it swallows a real failure

Run against **#1137** (`8791ba47`), the known offender -- it retimed the
historical event deck and edited `rarity_curves.json`, and its missing ladder
bump stood for 31 hours. A detached worktree at `8791ba47`, base `8791ba47^`,
running the code exactly as `main` has it:

```
$ bash -c 'python tools/check_ladder_bump.py --base 8791ba47^ || true; echo "wrapper exit=$?"'
[check_ladder_bump] WARNING: gameplay-surface files changed but ladder_version.txt was NOT bumped.
  ...
  Gameplay-surface files in this diff:
    - godot/data/events/balancing/rarity_curves.json
    - godot/data/events/overrides/README.md
    - godot/data/events/overrides/promotion_pass_2026_08.json

[check_ladder_bump] advisory mode: not failing the build. Reviewer must ack.
wrapper exit=0
```

Isolating the two layers:

```
$ bash -c 'python tools/check_ladder_bump.py --base 8791ba47^; echo "script exit=$?"'
... [same warning] ...
script exit=0

$ bash -c 'python tools/check_ladder_bump.py --base 8791ba47^ --strict >/dev/null; echo "strict exit=$?"'
strict exit=1
$ bash -c 'python tools/check_ladder_bump.py --base 8791ba47^ --strict >/dev/null || true; echo "strict+|| true wrapper exit=$?"'
strict+|| true wrapper exit=0
```

So: the script *can* fail, `--strict` makes it fail, and `|| true` un-fails it.

**Unflattering correction to the record.** The `v0.14.0` tag message (in
`public/releases/releases.json`) says the guard missed #1137 because
`GAMEPLAY_PREFIXES` excludes `godot/autoload/`, where the retime lives. The run
above shows that is not what happened: #1137 also touched
`godot/data/events/**`, which **is** in the allowlist, and the checker named
those files. The allowlist worked. The double-disarm is the whole reason nobody
saw it. The `godot/autoload/` gap is real but was not the cause here, and it is
out of scope for this PR.

## After: the same scenario, now failing

Same worktree, same range, with this branch's checker and the invocation CI now
uses (`--strict`, no `|| true`):

```
$ bash -c 'LADDER_ACK="" python tools/check_ladder_bump.py --base 8791ba47^ --strict; echo "CI step exit=$?"'
[check_ladder_bump] WARNING: gameplay-surface files changed but ladder_version.txt was NOT bumped.
  ...
  Gameplay-surface files in this diff:
    - godot/data/events/balancing/rarity_curves.json
    - godot/data/events/overrides/promotion_pass_2026_08.json

[check_ladder_bump] --strict: FAILING. The warning above is not a demand to bump --
  it is a demand that a human state, in writing, which case this is.
  To ack, do EITHER:
    - add a line to the PR body:  ladder-ack: <reason, at least 8 chars>
    - or apply the 'ladder-ack' label to the PR,
  then re-run this job. ...
CI step exit=1
```

Acked, it goes green -- and the reason is printed into the job log, so the
decision is recoverable later:

```
$ LADDER_ACK="ladder-ack: retimes the historical deck, forking to L4 in the release cut" \
  python tools/check_ladder_bump.py --base 8791ba47^ --strict
[check_ladder_bump] ACKED by reviewer via LADDER_ACK: retimes the historical deck, forking to L4 in the release cut
[check_ladder_bump] --strict: warning(s) acked in writing, passing.
CI step exit=0
```

And the clean case stays clean -- the `v0.14.0..HEAD` range (the `v0.14.1`
patch, which must NOT move the ladder):

```
$ LADDER_ACK="" python tools/check_ladder_bump.py --base v0.14.0 --strict
[check_ladder_bump] OK: 0 gameplay-surface file(s) changed, ladder_version.txt not bumped -- consistent.
CI step exit=0
```

## Why `|| true` was there -- determined, not guessed

`git log -S'|| true' -- .github/workflows/quality-checks.yml` returns exactly one
commit: **`e0963ca9`**, the commit that *introduced* the checker. It was born
disarmed, with the step named "Ladder Bump Heuristic (advisory)" and the inline
echo "Advisory smell detector, never blocks; reviewer acks against the spec
Section 3.3 checklist." It was **not** added later to suppress observed noise.

So the design intent was already right --
`BUILD_VS_LADDER_VERSION_SPLIT.md` 4.2 asks for "a WARNING **requiring an
explicit ack**". The ack half was never mechanised. `|| true` stood in for a
mechanism that did not exist.

## Why not simply delete `|| true`

Because the ladder moves **once per epoch, not once per PR** (L1..L4 across
hundreds of PRs). "Gameplay files changed and the ladder did not move" is the
*normal, correct* state of almost every gameplay PR. A bare hard-fail would go
red constantly and be switched back off within a week -- reproducing the
original failure with extra steps.

So this PR builds the missing ack:

- CI runs `--strict` and **no** `|| true`.
- A warning fails **unless** the PR body has a `ladder-ack: <reason>` line
  (reason >= 8 chars, so `ladder-ack: y` is not an ack) **or** the `ladder-ack`
  label is applied.
- The ack reason is echoed into the job log.
- PR body and labels are passed via `env:`, never interpolated inline -- matching
  the existing `BASE_REF` SECURITY comment.

## Two real false positives fixed, so the strict gate is not noisy

Removing `|| true` only holds if the check is not crying wolf. Two came out of
the runs above:

1. `*.md` under `godot/data/` -- the #1137 run flagged
   `godot/data/events/overrides/README.md` as gameplay surface. Prose in the
   `.pck` cannot move a score.
2. `godot/data/patch_notes.json` -- release copy read only by
   `godot/scripts/ui/whats_new_modal.gd`. It changes on **every** release, so
   leaving it in would demand an ack on every release PR. Kept as an explicit
   one-entry `EXCLUDE_PATHS` list rather than a pattern, so adding to it is a
   decision someone made.

I did **not** widen `GAMEPLAY_PREFIXES` to include `godot/autoload/` in this PR.
It is a genuine gap (`event_service.gd` lives there) but it is a separate change
with its own false-positive surface, and #1178 is about the guard being armed.

## Tests

New `tests/test_check_ladder_bump.py`, 13 tests, all passing:

```
$ python -m pytest tests/test_check_ladder_bump.py -q
.............                                                            [100%]
13 passed in 3.90s
```

The load-bearing ones assert the **exit codes**, so a future re-disarming shows
up as a red test rather than as a green job that checks nothing:
`test_gameplay_without_bump_fails_under_strict`,
`test_bump_without_gameplay_change_fails_under_strict`,
`test_token_ack_reason_is_not_an_ack`.

Pre-existing, unrelated: `tests/test_ascii_compliance.py` fails on
`docs/AGENT_EFFICIENCY_AUDIT.md` (non-ASCII at position 144) on `main` as well.
Not touched here.

`docs/TOOLS.md` regenerated (`check_ladder_bump.py` moves OBSERVE -> PROVE, and
picks up its new test as a discovered caller). No Godot code changed, so the
Godot fast gate is untouched by this diff.

## Note: other guards wearing the same clothes (NOT changed here)

`grep -n "|| true\|continue-on-error\|exit 0" .github/workflows/*.yml`. Reported
so it is written down, deliberately out of scope for #1178:

| Location | What it does | Read |
|---|---|---|
| `godot-tests.yml:37` | `godot --headless --path godot --import \|\| true` | Probably fine -- the import pass floods stderr by design (CLAUDE.md); the real gate is the test run after it. Worth a second look. |
| `data-validation.yml:59` | `validate_historical_data.py --verbose > report.txt 2>&1 \|\| true` | **Same shape as #1178.** A validator whose exit code is discarded into a report file. Highest-value follow-up on this list. |
| `docs-sync.yml:42` | `continue-on-error: true` | Sync step; low stakes. |
| `enhanced-release.yml:50, :434` | `continue-on-error: true` | On the RELEASE path. Worth reading -- release-path softness is what this repo keeps getting bitten by. |
| `godot-tests.yml:186, :272` | `continue-on-error: true` | Both annotated with a reason (artifact upload / PR-comment API hiccup), and `:126` explicitly notes it does NOT use `continue-on-error` for the gate itself. This is the pattern the others should copy. |
| `live-site-release-freshness.yml:104,153,158`; `release-sync-monitor.yml:42,49,53,63`; `sync-documentation.yml:64` | bare `exit 0` | Early-outs on "nothing to check" branches; need reading one by one to tell a legitimate skip from a swallowed failure. Not audited here. |

Filing these as a note, not a PR. If they want chasing, they want their own
issue -- `data-validation.yml:59` first.

issues.title: fix(test-gate): a timed-out run is NO RESULT, not "0 tests, 0 fail (FAIL)" (#1181)
issues.body:
Closes #1181. Partially addresses #1168 (asks 1 and 2; ask 3 is a different defect -- see below).

## What the runner reported at the cap BEFORE this change

`scripts/run_godot_tests.py:375` had `timeout=900` hardcoded, and the timeout branch returned `(False, 0, 0, [])`. Those zeros were then rendered by the reporting layer as if they were measurements.

Reproduced deterministically without launching Godot, by replacing `subprocess.run` with a stub that raises `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` exactly as it would after 900s, so the real timeout branch and the real reporting path execute:

```
[TEST] Running 'quick' tests in res://tests/unit (1 files on disk)

[FAIL] Tests timed out after 15 minutes!

============================================================
[TOTALS] quick: 0 tests, 0 fail (FAIL)
[FAILURE] Gate failed (see above).
============================================================

--- markdown summary CI would render ---

### Godot test results

| Suite | Tests | Failures | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| quick | 0 | 0 | FAIL |

--- process would sys.exit(1) ---
```

**Two findings, one of which corrects the issue title.**

1. It did **not** exit zero and did **not** read as a pass. Exit was 1 and the word was `FAIL`. The issue title's "reports a timeout as `0 tests, 0 fail (FAIL)`" is exactly right; anyone reading it as "looks green" would be wrong, and that is worth stating because it bounds the damage.
2. The real defect is that a run which produced **no measurement** was rendered in the identical shape to one that did. No JUnit file was ever written -- nothing ran, nothing passed, nothing failed -- yet the output asserts `0 tests` and `0 fail`. Both are fabricated. `0 fail` is literally true and completely misleading.

That is #640's defect (the gate reporting a number that did not come from tests executing) reappearing inside the runner written to prevent it, with the sign flipped. It matters most in the CI step summary, where the simulation tier is non-blocking: a timeout there renders as `| simulation (non-blocking) | 0 | 0 | FAIL |`, one quiet row that a reader has to already know how to distrust.

## What changed

- **`--timeout SECONDS`**, env fallback **`PDOOM1_TEST_TIMEOUT`**, `0` removes the cap. Default stays **900** -- the previously-hardcoded value -- so CI's contract is byte-identical. A unit test pins that default so a future change to it has to be deliberate.
- The resolved cap **and its provenance** are printed before each run (`[TIMEOUT] Per-run wall-clock cap: 900s (from default).`). An implicit cap that silently destroys a measurement is the thing being fixed; the reader should never have to guess which number was in force.
- **Three outcomes rather than two**: `PASS` / `FAIL` / `NO RESULT`, exit `0` / `1` / `2`. A `NO RESULT` row carries `tests=None, failures=None`, so there is no number available to print anywhere. `NO RESULT` outranks `FAIL` in the exit code: if a tier did not run, the most important thing to tell the caller is that the run cannot be reported on.
- The `NO RESULT` path also covers "the Godot process could not be run at all". The deliberate hard-failure paths from #629/#590 (missing dir, no test files, unparseable JUnit) are left as `FAIL` -- unchanged.
- 13 unit tests in `tests/test_run_godot_tests_timeout.py`, mostly **negative** assertions: the totals line must not contain `0 tests` or `0 fail`, the markdown must not contain `| 0 | 0 |`, the outcome must not equal `FAIL` or `PASS`.
- Doc section in `docs/TESTING_QUALITY_GATES.md`; `docs/TOOLS.md` regenerated by its own generator.

## Proof: the cap now reports unmistakably, and exits non-zero

Real Godot 4.5.1, this branch, isolated `APPDATA`, `--timeout 5`:

```
[TIMEOUT] Per-run wall-clock cap: 5s (from --timeout).

[TEST] Running 'quick' tests in res://tests/unit (126 files on disk)

!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
[NO RESULT] 'quick': TIMED OUT after 5s (cap 5s).
[NO RESULT] No JUnit file was written, so there is NO test count for
[NO RESULT] this run: nothing passed and nothing failed. This is NOT a
[NO RESULT] green run and NOT a measured failure -- it is an absence of
[NO RESULT] measurement. Do not report a suite result from it.
[NO RESULT] Fix: --timeout N / PDOOM1_TEST_TIMEOUT=N (0 removes the cap).
!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

============================================================
[TOTALS] quick: NO RESULT -- run did not complete, no test count exists
[NO RESULT] quick did not run to completion. This is NOT a pass and NOT a test failure -- no measurement exists. Do not report a suite result from this run.
            quick: killed by the 5s wall-clock cap after 5s, before GUT wrote any results. Raise the cap with --timeout N (or PDOOM1_TEST_TIMEOUT=N), or --timeout 0 to remove it.
============================================================
EXIT=2
```

And the markdown CI would render (via `PDOOM1_TEST_TIMEOUT=4 ... --summary`, which also demonstrates the env var):

```
## [!] QUICK DID NOT COMPLETE -- NO RESULT

`quick` was killed by the 4s wall-clock cap after 4s, before GUT wrote any results. Raise the cap with --timeout N (or PDOOM1_TEST_TIMEOUT=N), or --timeout 0 to remove it. No test count exists for this run: it is neither a pass nor a failure. Treat this tier as UNMEASURED and do not quote a suite result from it.

### Godot test results

| Suite | Tests | Failures | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| quick | - | - | **NO RESULT (did not run)** |
```

## Proof: a normal run still passes

```
$ python scripts/run_godot_tests.py --quick --ci-mode --min-tests 300 --summary

[TIMEOUT] Per-run wall-clock cap: 900s (from default).

[TEST] Running 'quick' tests in res://tests/unit (126 files on disk)

[PASS] 'quick': 1250 tests, 0 failures, 126/126 files collected.

| Suite | Tests | Failures | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| quick | 1250 | 0 | PASS |

============================================================
[TOTALS] quick: 1250 tests, 0 fail (ok)
[SUCCESS] All requested suites passed the gate! CHECKED
============================================================
EXIT=0
```

Python tests: `13 passed`.

## Is #1168 the same root cause?

**Half of it.** #1168 lists three asks. Asks 1 (`--timeout` flag) and 2 (a timeout must report as UNKNOWN / DID NOT RUN, never `0 tests, 0 fail`) are the same two defects as #1181 and are fixed here -- same file, same lines, same code path.

Ask 3 is **not** the same root cause and is not touched: *why* the simulation tier takes >1630s on Windows while Ubuntu CI finishes it in 460-550s. That is a Godot/GUT/test-content performance question (#1168 has a partial diagnosis: 16.2 min wall clock against 7.9s user CPU, so blocked on I/O, and the per-RNG-draw `[VerificationTracker]` print is the suspect -- with the caveat, stated in the issue, that redirecting stdout to a file did not fix it). Nothing in this PR makes that faster. It makes the tier **obtainable** locally by letting the cap be raised, which is the difference between "no result is possible on this machine" and "a result costs 30 minutes".

So: **#1168 should stay open** after this merges, retitled or scoped down to ask 3 alone.

## Deliberately not done

- The default is still 900. Changing it silently alters CI for everyone and belongs in its own reviewed decision.
- No environment-dependent default (e.g. a longer cap when `CI` is unset). Tempting, and it would make the Windows case work with no flag, but it forks behaviour between machines on an implicit signal -- the opposite of what this issue is about.
- No streaming stall-detector. `capture_output=False` already streams GUT's output live, so "slow" and "hung" are separable by watching; making the *runner* able to tell them apart is worth doing, but it belongs with #1168 ask 3 where the measurement is.

## Note for the reviewer: a duplicate lane

There is a second, uncommitted attempt at this same issue in the worktree `C:/Users/Pip/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/wt-1181` on branch `fix/1181-sim-timeout-flag` -- ~420 insertions, no commits, no PR, last modified 06:41 and untouched for 36 minutes when this lane started. Flagging it so it is not reviewed twice or lost silently. Its approach differs in one way worth a decision either way: it makes the local default 2700s for the simulation tier while keeping 900 in CI, gated on the `CI` env var. This PR does not, for the reason under "Deliberately not done".

issues.title: ci(ladder): arm check_ladder_bump.py, and prove it can fail (#1178)
issues.body:
Closes #1178.

`quality-checks.yml` ran `check_ladder_bump.py` with `|| true`, so it was
structurally incapable of failing a build. This makes it correct, makes it able
to see an epoch cut, and then removes the `|| true`.

## The old gate's record, re-measured over real history

I re-ran `origin/main`'s script (with `--strict`) over the actual commits:

| range | old gate | correct answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `#1137` historical-deck retime (`8791ba47`) | WARN, invisible behind `\|\| true` | WARN |
| `#1101` net fix in `godot/autoload/event_service.gd` (`d7b47a1a`) | **OK -- blind** | WARN |
| v0.14.0 epoch cut (`7368e237`) | **WARN -- wrong** | OK |
| v0.14.1 patch cut (`0dc8adb9`) | **WARN -- wrong** | OK |

**Correction to the issue text, row 1.** The old `GAMEPLAY_PREFIXES` included
`godot/data/`, and `#1137` also changed `godot/data/events/balancing/rarity_curves.json`
and added `promotion_pass_2026_08.json`. So the old gate DID flag `#1137` -- via
the data files, not the autoload file. What hid it for 31 hours was `|| true`,
not the allowlist. The allowlist gap is real and independently fatal, which is
what row 2 shows: an event-scheduling change in `godot/autoload/event_service.gd`
that the old gate called clean.

Row 4 is a false positive the issue did not know about: `godot/data/patch_notes.json`
is player-facing copy, ships in every patch, and sits inside the wholesale
`godot/data/` prefix.

## 1. Making it correct

Polarity inverted. **Gameplay is the DEFAULT inside `godot/`**, with an explicit
cosmetic denylist: `scenes/`, `scripts/ui/`, `assets/`, `theme/`, `tests/`,
`scripts/dev|debug/`, `addons/`, `tools/`, `docs/`, plus `patch_notes.json`,
`credits.json`, `icon_mapping.json`, `project.godot`, `export_presets.cfg`,
`build_stamp.txt`, and `.md`/`.uid`/`.import`.

An allowlist has to enumerate every gameplay directory in advance, so it is wrong
the first time a system moves -- which is exactly what happened. The costs are
asymmetric: a missed bump silently merges scores earned under different rules and
cannot be undone once played; a spurious flag costs one line in a commit message.

`godot/autoload/game_config.gd` is judged by its **changed lines**, not its path.
It is real gameplay surface (`effective_difficulty()`, the league difficulty lock)
and also a `sync_version.py` stamp target, so every release cut touches it. If the
only lines that moved are `CURRENT_VERSION`, `LADDER_VERSION`, `INTRO_VERSION` or
`FEATURED_SEED_OVERRIDE`, that is not evidence of a gameplay change.

### Where the code and `BUILD_VS_LADDER_VERSION_SPLIT.md` disagreed

All three are recorded in a new spec section 4.2a. The code faithfully implemented
Section 4.2; Section 4.2 disagrees with Sections 3.1 and 3.2.

1. **The allowlist cannot reach the spec's own triggers.** Section 3.1 makes
   "anything that changes which events fire on a given seed" a bump trigger. The
   Section 4.2 allowlist (`godot/scripts/core/**`, `godot/data/**`,
   `seed_schedule.gd`, "scoring files") excludes `godot/autoload/`, where
   `event_service.gd` (event scheduling) and `balance.gd` live.
2. **`godot/data/**` wholesale contradicts Section 3.2**, which lists "copy/text,
   patch notes" as explicitly non-bumping. That is the v0.14.1 false positive.
3. **`seed_schedule.gd` as a loose basename was redundant** -- the file is at
   `godot/scripts/core/seed_schedule.gd`, already inside the allowlist.

One case neither 3.1 nor 3.2 covers, now ruled in 4.2a and open to argument:
**rolling `FEATURED_SEED_OVERRIDE` is NOT a bump trigger.** It changes which seed
is featured, not what happens on any given seed -- it starts a new board by SEED,
not a new epoch.

## 2. Making it see an epoch cut

When a diff bumps the ladder, the question is not "did this PR change gameplay" --
an epoch cut is version-files-only by construction and never does. The gate now
looks back over the **epoch window**: the last commit that changed
`ladder_version.txt` before this range, through HEAD. For v0.14.0 that window is
`9abe20a7..7368e237`, which contains `#1137`.

Argued against the alternatives: comparing against the last *tag* would break for
epoch bumps that do not coincide with a release (`9abe20a7`, the 3-office lease
PR, bumped L2 -> L3 mid-cycle); a marker alone would put the burden on the person
least able to remember it, at cut time, at the end of a release day.

**What the epoch window misses:**

- It proves the epoch contains SOME gameplay change, not that it contains the one
  that justified the bump.
- It needs full git history back to the previous bump. `actions/checkout` now uses
  `fetch-depth: 0`. On a shallow clone where the previous epoch is unreachable, the
  epoch-window check is SKIPPED with a loud message rather than passing quietly.
- Epoch 1 has no predecessor; that case is reported, not failed.

## 3. The declaration, and why arming needed it

26 of the 81 first-parent commits since `v0.13.2` touch gameplay directories, and
only 2 bumped the ladder. Arming direction 1 without an escape hatch would hard-fail
roughly one PR in three -- comment edits and refactors inside `core/` are legitimate
no-bumps.

So a deliberate no-bump must be **stated**, in a commit message or the PR body:

```
Ladder-Impact: none -- comment-only edit, no reachable behaviour change
Ladder-Impact: bump -- reorders an RNG draw in a UI path
```

The PR body reaches the script through the `LADDER_DECLARATION_TEXT` env var (never
inline in the shell -- it is user-controlled text). `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`
carries both lines commented out.

This is the point rather than a workaround: the gate cannot decide whether a diff
changes behaviour, and pretending otherwise is what produced two useless signals.
It can insist a human answered, somewhere git preserves and the release cut can
read. **It does not verify the answer** -- a false `Ladder-Impact: none` passes.

## The acceptance runs (actual output)

**RED on the real miss (`#1137`):**

```
$ python tools/check_ladder_bump.py --base 8791ba47^ --head 8791ba47
[check_ladder_bump] FAIL: gameplay-surface files changed, ladder_version.txt was NOT bumped,
  and no Ladder-Impact declaration was found.
  ...
  Gameplay-surface files in this diff:
    - godot/autoload/event_service.gd
    - godot/data/events/balancing/rarity_curves.json
    - godot/data/events/overrides/promotion_pass_2026_08.json
exit=1
```

**GREEN on the real epoch cut (v0.14.0):**

```
$ python tools/check_ladder_bump.py --base 7368e237^ --head 7368e237
[check_ladder_bump] epoch window 9abe20a7..7368e237: 59 gameplay-surface file(s) changed
  since the previous epoch -- the bump is justified.
[check_ladder_bump] OK: 0 gameplay-surface file(s) changed, ladder_version.txt bumped -- consistent.
exit=0
```

Note "0 gameplay-surface file(s) changed" in the cut itself: the pass comes from
the epoch window, not from the `FEATURED_SEED_OVERRIDE` line that happens to ride
along on this particular cut. That line is excluded on purpose, so the test proves
the epoch-window fix rather than passing on a decoy.

**GREEN on the real patch cut (v0.14.1, ladder stayed 4):**

```
$ python tools/check_ladder_bump.py --base 0dc8adb9^ --head 0dc8adb9
[check_ladder_bump] OK: 0 gameplay-surface file(s) changed, ladder_version.txt not bumped -- consistent.
exit=0
```

**Direction 2 proven red** against a synthetic commit that bumps
`ladder_version.txt` alone on top of `7368e237` (an epoch window with no gameplay
in it):

```
[check_ladder_bump] FAIL: ladder_version.txt was bumped, but NO gameplay-surface file has
  changed since the previous epoch (7368e237).
exit=1
```

## The gate proves itself on every build

`--self-test` replays all four rows of the table and fails if the gate stops going
red on the two misses or starts crying wolf on the two release cuts. It runs in
`quality-checks.yml` on every build, in the same job that arms the gate:

```
[self-test] 4 case(s) ran, 0 mismatch(es), 0 skipped.
[self-test] PASS: red on both real misses, green on both real release cuts.
```

If zero cases can run (shallow history), `--self-test` FAILS rather than reporting
a green it did not earn. That is the #640 lesson: a guard that has never been shown
to fail is not evidence.

## Still not caught

- An RNG-stream change inside a denylisted cosmetic path. The golden-replay
  determinism backstop (spec 4.2, slow tier) remains the only real answer.
- A false `Ladder-Impact: none`.
- Whether the gameplay change in an epoch window is the one that justified the bump.

## Not touched

`version.txt`, `ladder_version.txt`, tags, and everything under `godot/`.
`CHANGELOG.md` and `scripts/run_godot_tests.py` left alone for the `#1165` / `#1181`
lanes. `docs/TOOLS.md` moved by one line because the pre-commit generator saw the
tool's `Layer:` change from OBSERVE to PROVE.

Ladder-Impact: none -- CI tooling and docs only, nothing under godot/ changed

issues.title: run_godot_tests.py: the 900s sim cap has no flag, and reports a timeout as '0 tests, 0 fail (FAIL)'
issues.body:
## What happened

Cutting v0.14.1, the simulation tier could not be measured locally. `run_godot_tests.py --simulation` timed out and printed:

```
[FAIL] Tests timed out after 15 minutes!
[TOTALS] simulation: 0 tests, 0 fail (FAIL)
[FAILURE] Gate failed (see above).
```

CI ran the identical tree green in **7m45s**. A direct GUT invocation outside the runner, on the same machine and worktree, was **still progressing at 27m10s** when it was killed -- live `[VerificationTracker] RNG:` traces throughout, so slow, not hung.

## Why this is the hollow-CI shape again

`0 tests, 0 fail (FAIL)` is a report about a run that never produced a result, rendered in the same shape as a run that produced one. Issue #640 fixed exactly this class on the CI side: the gate reported a number that did not come from tests actually executing. The timeout path reintroduces it locally, with the sign flipped -- #640 said "green while running zero tests", this says "FAIL while running an unknown number of tests". Both make the count meaningless, and neither tells the reader which it is.

The practical consequence tonight: a release had to be cut on CI's measurement alone, and the honest release note had to say so.

## The cap

`scripts/run_godot_tests.py:375`

```python
timeout=900,
```

Hardcoded, no flag, no env override. CI needs ~460-550s; this dev box needs >1630s (contention: concurrent agent lanes, an art generation wave, multiple Godot instances). There is no value that is right for both machines, which is the argument for it being a parameter rather than a better constant.

## Suggested shape (not prescriptive)

- `--timeout SECONDS` with the current 900 as the default, so CI's contract is unchanged.
- Distinguish the outcomes in the report. A timeout is not `0 tests, 0 fail (FAIL)`; it is `TIMED OUT after Ns, no result`. The min-tests floor from #640 already proves the runner knows the difference between "ran and passed" and "did not run".
- Consider streaming GUT progress so slow and hung are separable without watching the process list. Tonight that took a `tasklist` check on RSS.

## Not fixed inside the release

Deliberately left alone while cutting v0.14.1 -- changing the test runner during a release is the wrong time to find out the change was wrong.

## Provenance

Measured 2026-08-08 cutting v0.14.1 at `0dc8adb9`, worktree `wt-rel1411`, Godot 4.5.1-stable, isolated `APPDATA`.

issues.title: check_ladder_bump.py runs with '|| true' -- the guard on the board-key invariant cannot fail, and it already missed one for 31 hours
issues.body:
**Verified 2026-08-08 01:45, raised by the `pdoom1-website` seat during the `v0.14.1` prep and confirmed here by reading the file.**

## The finding

`.github/workflows/quality-checks.yml:79`

```yaml
python tools/check_ladder_bump.py --base "origin/$BASE_REF" || true
```

**`|| true` means this check cannot fail a build.** It prints, and the job goes green regardless of what it found.

## Why it matters more than a normal disarmed guard

**This is the guard on the one invariant that makes the whole build-vs-ladder split work.** `docs/game-design/BUILD_VS_LADDER_VERSION_SPLIT.md` exists so that a change altering which events fire on a given seed cannot ship without forking the board. Board key is `(seed, ladder_version)`. **If the ladder moves silently, scores land on a board built under different rules and the leaderboard is quietly wrong** — which is exactly the reasoning that justified last night's L3 → L4 fork.

**It has already missed one.** 67 commits sat between `v0.13.2` and the `v0.14.0` cut without the ladder being bumped, including `#1137`, which retimed the historical event deck and modified `rarity_curves.json` — a textbook BUMP trigger under §3.1. **A human caught it at cut time, not the check.** The `pdoom1-website` seat reports the miss stood for **31 hours**.

**And it is live tonight.** `v0.14.1` is a patch and **must not move the ladder**; the board key must stay `(weekly-2026-w32, L4)`. The check that would catch a fork wearing a patch number is the one that cannot fail.

## This is `5g`, exactly

*A guard that has never failed is not evidence, it is a claim about a guard.* pdoom1's own origin story is CI reporting green while running zero tests. **`|| true` is that, deliberately configured.**

## Suggested fix, and the reason it is not simply "remove `|| true`"

Removing it makes every PR that legitimately does not bump the ladder fail, if the checker's default is to complain. So:

1. **Establish what the checker currently returns** on a no-bump-needed PR and on a bump-needed PR. If it already exits 0 / non-zero correctly, `|| true` is pure suppression — **delete it.**
2. If it does not, fix the checker's exit codes first, then delete `|| true`.
3. **Per `coordination#5g`: show it RED against the live defect before declaring it fixed.** `#1137` is a known real offender sitting in history — run the checker against that range and confirm it names it. A guard proven red against a real case is evidence; a guard that has only ever been green is a claim.

## Closing observation (write-once)

```bash
grep -n "check_ladder_bump" .github/workflows/quality-checks.yml   # no '|| true'
# AND, recorded in the PR: the red run naming #1137 or an equivalent real offender,
# with its output, alongside the green run on a clean branch.
```

**Both runs reported with real numbers**, not just the green one.

issues.title: fix(leaderboard): the Operator name was collected and never carried anywhere -- two identity fields, and a truncation that stops amputating
issues.body:
Branched from `fix/leaderboard-visibility-set` (PR #1173, still open at time of writing), not from `main`.

## What the board displays today vs what is collected

Measured against the live `(weekly-2026-w32, L4)` board on 2026-08-08, not assumed:

| | Collected by the game | Reaches the board |
|---|---|---|
| Operator name (`GameConfig.player_name`, default `"Researcher"`) | Yes -- persisted, loaded, settable, and asked for by the #1133 prompt under the label `Operator:` | **No. Nowhere. No code path ever moved it.** |
| Lab name (`GameConfig.lab_name`) | Yes, with a generator and a Reroll button | Yes -- in a field named `player_name` |

The receiving field declared itself:

```gdscript
var player_name: String  # Lab name
```

A field whose own comment admitted it was misnamed, feeding a public column of the same wrong name. That is the silent-wrongness pattern in a schema, and the website renders that column.

`docs/LEADERBOARD_WEBSITE_INTEGRATION.md:148` documented the same thing as if it were fine: `` `player_name` | string | Lab name displayed on leaderboard ``.

## The truncation limit: 40 bytes, measured

I did not trust the figure of 40. I fetched the live board and measured it:

```
GET https://api.pdoom1.com/score_api.php?seed=weekly-2026-w32&version=L4&limit=50

'GRIM (Global Risk Intervention Mechanism'  len=40   <- Pip, amputated
'GRIM'                                      len=4
'GRIM'                                      len=4
''                                          len=0
''                                          len=0
```

Submitted `"GRIM (Global Risk Intervention Mechanism)"` = 41 bytes. Stored = 40. **The server ate exactly one byte, silently.** The limit is 40, confirmed by the boundary rather than by the doc.

Two things that measurement adds beyond the number:

- The cut is **byte-wise**. A non-ASCII name (a player typing an accented name) can be split mid-codepoint and stored as invalid UTF-8. Fitting client-side prevents that too.
- **Two of the five live rows have an EMPTY name.** `_has_submittable_identity()` requires both fields non-empty, so those rows did not come through the current consent path. I have not chased this; flagging it as unexplained, not fixed.

`score_api.php` is deployed server-side and is **not in `pdoom1-website` or any repo on this machine** (I checked). The only truncation code in that repo is `bug-submit.php`, unrelated. So the limit cannot be raised from here.

## The decision, and what I did with it

Pip ruled mid-task, so this PR builds the answer rather than a card:

> "can we submit both? players will collide on lab names and player names are also cool because then a player can have different labs?"

**BOTH, as separate values.** Lab names collide -- that is *why* the #1133 generator exists -- so a lab alone cannot identify a person; and one Operator running several labs over several months is a feature that a single conflated field would destroy permanently.

He also said *"I'm not asking for it now it just feels silly"* -- naming the absurdity, not setting a deadline. So this PR stops short of anything that migrates live data or needs a server change.

## What is implemented

1. **The field name and its contents now agree.** `ScoreEntry.player_name` -> `ScoreEntry.lab_name`, plus a new `ScoreEntry.operator_name`. The old name is **gone, not repurposed** -- a stale reader errors loudly instead of silently returning the wrong name. Two pre-existing tests broke on exactly that, which is the property working rather than a regression.

   The JSON **key** stays `player_name`, because every local board file on disk and every row on the live board uses it. The GDScript field is honest; the wire key is the frozen contract, now documented as misnamed.

2. **Truncation is legible and client-side.** `Leaderboard.fit_board_name()` -- pure, static, unit-tested -- fits to the measured 40-byte budget, cutting on a word boundary and marking the cut with ASCII `...`. Applied in `to_wire_dict()`, so the server's `substr` never fires.

   Pip's lab now goes up as `GRIM (Global Risk Intervention...` instead of `GRIM (Global Risk Intervention Mechanism`.

   A name that fits passes through untouched -- a cut mark on an uncut name is its own small lie.

3. **The prompt no longer overpromises.** `IDENTITY_PROMPT_BOARD_NOTE` states that the global board shows the Lab name and the Operator name is saved with the run locally. The prompt was collecting two values while one of them went nowhere.

4. **Local/remote split made explicit.** `to_dict()` = the full local record (both names). `to_wire_dict()` = exactly the frozen server contract, name pre-fitted, `operator_name` **deliberately omitted**.

## What I deliberately did NOT do

- **Did not send `operator_name` on the wire.** The server's tolerance for unknown keys is unmeasured and a rejected POST loses a score. Sending it blind at 01:00 against a live public board is the wrong trade.
- **Did not touch a single row on the live board.**
- **Did not render both names on the leaderboard screen.** Remote rows will never carry an operator until the server does, so the screen would render a ragged mix.
- No `version.txt` / `ladder_version.txt` / tag change. Ladder stays L4; the board key does not move. Nothing here touches RNG, economy or replay determinism.

## What happens to the rows already on the live board

`from_dict` defaults `operator_name` to `""` for any row lacking it -- which is every row that exists today, local and remote.

- Existing rows present as **lab-only, rendered honestly**. No backfill.
- Backfilling the lab into the operator field would **fabricate an identity** -- asserting that a human is named "GRIM". There is a test asserting it does not happen.
- Pip's amputated row stays amputated. Fixing it is a server-side edit; only future submissions are fitted.

## Open, for coordination (pdoom1-website / API territory)

1. **Add a second identity field to the score API** (schema + endpoint + public rendering) so the Operator name can be carried. This PR has the client value sitting ready.
2. **Either raise the 40-byte limit or make the server's cut legible**, and return the stored value so the client can tell the player what actually landed. The client now fits to 40 regardless.
3. **Why do two live rows have empty names?** Unexplained.

Written up in `docs/LEADERBOARD_WEBSITE_INTEGRATION.md` so it survives this PR.

issues.title: art(l2): bridge the review state to the runner and fire the L2 wave -- 306 images, USD 15.30
issues.body:
The L2 wave of the 2026-08-07 art night ran. 306 images, USD 15.30 from the
ledger, zero failures. This PR is the code and data that made it possible plus
the two prompt fixes it exposed; the images themselves are under
`art_generated/`, which is gitignored in full.

## What `--picks` actually wanted

`run_art_night.py --picks tools/art_review/review_state.json` returned
`[ABORT] L2 needs picks and none parsed`. Two independent mismatches, and
neither one raised anything:

1. **Shape.** `load_picks`' dict branch expects `{id: [tag, tag]}` -- a list of
   tag strings per id. `review_state.json` stores
   `{id: {"verdict":..., "tags":[], "note":..., "updated_at":...}}`. Iterating
   that value yields the field names `verdict`/`tags`/`note`/`updated_at`, none
   of which are in `FAVOURABLE_TAGS`, so all 5794 entries read as
   non-favourable. Not a crash -- a shrug.
2. **Vocabulary.** `FAVOURABLE_TAGS` is
   `{love, like, promote, favour, favor, hero, yes, keep}`. `iterate` is not in
   it, and `iterate` is exactly the verdict L2 exists to consume.

**Bridge:** `load_picks` accepts a second shape -- a flat JSON list of ids,
taken verbatim with no tag filtering. New `tools/art_review/export_picks.py`
emits that. Verdict policy therefore lives in the review layer where it is
readable and arguable, instead of widening the runner's tag vocabulary and
quietly making `keep` mean "vary this".

## Which picks, and what was excluded

Fed: the **51** parseable `iterate` verdicts on the `an0807` batch.

| bucket | n | fed? | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `an0807` iterate, scene cells | 51 | yes | "this direction is right, vary it" -- literally L2's input |
| `an0807` iterate, L0 swatch sheets | 5 | no | cell key is a bare palette id (`p01`); no subject/rendering/palette triple to vary. Dropped **and printed**. |
| `an0807` keep | 143 | no | a keep says "this image is good", not "vary this". That is an L3 signal. |
| iterate on pre-art-night batches | 70 | no | filenames are not art-night cells; `load_picks` cannot resolve them at all |
| all keeps corpus-wide | 3837 | no | 3837 x 6 steps x USD 0.05 = USD 1151, roughly 15x the whole ceiling |

`picks_target` raised **36 -> 51**. At 36 the runner would have silently thrown
away 15 of Pip's verdicts. It is also the difference between clearing the run's
own underspend floor and not:

| picks | L2 USD | run after L3 | vs floor 68.00 | headroom left |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 36 (old) | 10.80 | 66.25 | **missed** -- needs a topup wave | 9.25 |
| 51 (this) | 15.30 | 70.75 | met | 4.75 |

## Fixes this exposed

- **`load_picks` truncation is no longer silent.** It now prints when
  `picks_target` drops picks. Same class of wrongness as the tag bug.
- **Text leak, one mechanical cause found.** `poster_props` literally requested
  lettering: *"keyboards with worn legends"* -- legends are the printed
  characters on keycaps. Now blank keycaps. `poster_base`'s no-text clause also
  names the objects that really carry printing (binder spines, whiteboards,
  warning plates, rubber stamps, cartons, screens, keycaps) and offers a
  non-letterform fallback. Both clauses sit at the same prompt position and are
  constant across all 6 steps of a pick, so the within-pick axis comparison is
  unaffected. Only an L1-to-L2 comparison is contaminated, and generation
  lineage is a measured null.
- **`apply_review.py` Hold entries for the 7 L2 batches.** Without them
  `build_full_gallery.py` refuses to build -- correctly, since a review pass
  would strand its own keeps.

## Result, read from the ledger not the plan

- 306 ok / 0 failed / 0 stopped at ceiling, USD 15.30
- run total **USD 46.75 of 75.50**; **USD 28.75 left** against L3's USD 24.00
- 306 masters, 306 provenance sidecars, each with prompt sha256, model, size,
  quality, tariff cost, UTC timestamp, taste-brief sha256 (spot-checked, not
  assumed)
- axis coverage 48/48/42/42/42/42/42 across yaw, pitch, distance, title space,
  decay, quiet, style tween
- gallery rebuilt: 61 batches, 6511 assets; the `node --check` gate reported
  method `node --check`, so it genuinely parsed rather than falling back to the
  regex scanner

**What would prove this wrong:** tariff dollars are the published price, not
billed truth. Reconcile against the OpenAI billing dashboard before quoting the
spend anywhere it matters.
