issues.title: Ladder eligibility must be visible BEFORE the run starts, not delivered at death (ruled by Pip 2026-08-07)
issues.body:
**Ruling by Pip, 2026-08-07 ~23:30, during the v0.14.0 playtest:**

> "If we're setting up a game that isn't eligible for a ladder submission, we should know before we start the game"

## The rule

**Ladder eligibility is a property the player can see BEFORE committing to a run, not a verdict delivered at death.**

Today a run's eligibility is only surfaced at game over (`game_over_screen.gd:266`), and mid-run at first Alpha Tools use. Both are after the player has invested. Pip invested **147 turns** tonight before discovering a run produced nothing -- and the current design gives a player no way to know in advance.

## Why this is not just a nicety

Eligibility is already determined by state that exists **before turn 1**:

- `GameConfig.scenario_id` -- chosen pre-game
- difficulty (locked to Standard for league runs, #1058)
- the board key `(seed, ladder_epoch)` -- both known at setup
- Alpha Tools is the only input that arrives mid-run, and it is one-way, so "eligible so far" is honest and never becomes eligible again

So the information exists at setup. Nothing is being computed early; it is simply not being shown.

**And it would have made tonight's blocker visible in seconds instead of hours.** A pre-game readout would have told Pip immediately which of his three runs the game believed were rankable, splitting "the run was unranked" from "the submit path is broken" without any code reading at all. An eligibility indicator is a diagnostic instrument as much as a UI feature.

## What this asks for

1. **A clear, non-decorative eligibility statement on the pre-game / setup screen**, before the player commits. Something a person reads without hunting: whether this run will count, and if not, why not, in one line.
2. **Consistency with the existing tellings.** Alpha Tools already warns at the toggle, at first use, and at game over (decision card 2026-08-01). This adds a fourth position -- BEFORE -- and it should use the same vocabulary so a player reads one concept, not four.
3. **The honest wording problem worth designing around:** at setup the truthful statement is conditional -- "this run is eligible, and will stop being eligible if you use dev tools". Avoid promising a submission that a later action revokes. Pip's own standing preference is that the player should be told what is prevented and why, in plain words.

## Scope note

This is a DESIGN issue, filed separately from the live blocker (a clean 147-turn run submitting nothing, under diagnosis). **Do not let this absorb that.** If the diagnosis finds the submit path is broken, fixing it does not discharge this issue, and vice versa -- one is a defect, this is a missing affordance, and either could exist without the other.

## Related

- `game_over_screen.gd:266` -- current, and only, player-facing eligibility gate
- `GameConfig.is_ranked_run()` / `effective_difficulty()` -- the named accessors this would read
- `#1058` -- difficulty locked to Standard for comparable league runs
- `#1060` -- scenarios lock you out of the board, with an explicit pre-pick warning. **That warning is the precedent this generalises**: scenarios already tell the player before they commit. Alpha Tools and everything else do not.

issues.title: Simulation tier cannot be run locally on Windows -- 15-min hardcoded timeout, and a timeout reports as '0 tests, 0 fail'
issues.body:
Found while cutting v0.14.0 / L4, on the one release where the simulation tier is
the tier that matters (the cut forks the ladder because #1137 retimed the event
deck, and replay/determinism is exactly what this tier guards).

## The measurement

`python scripts/run_godot_tests.py --simulation --ci-mode --min-tests 80` on the
Windows dev machine, in a clean worktree at `origin/main` (`1795cd12`):

```
[TEST] Running 'simulation' tests in res://tests/unit/simulation (8 files on disk)
[FAIL] Tests timed out after 15 minutes!
[TOTALS] simulation: 0 tests, 0 fail (FAIL)
```

Run three times, ~15 min each:

| tree | stdout | result |
|---|---|---|
| v0.14.0 release branch | pipe | timeout, 0 tests |
| v0.14.0 release branch | redirected to a file | timeout, 0 tests |
| **unmodified `origin/main`** | redirected to a file | **timeout, 0 tests** |

The third row is the point: **main alone reproduces it.** The epoch cut is
exonerated by that A/B. This is pre-existing.

Meanwhile the same tier is **green in GitHub Actions on Ubuntu**, including on
the #1137 commit itself (run `31091011227`, job "Simulation Tests") and on the
latest main run (`31130859770`). The workflow passes `--min-tests 80`, so a
zero-test run would have failed the job; it did not.

## Two separate defects

**1. The tier cannot be run locally on Windows at all.**
15 minutes is hardcoded -- `scripts/run_godot_tests.py:329`,
`subprocess.run(..., timeout=900)` -- with no CLI flag to raise it. So a
developer on this machine has no way to get a result, only a timeout. Every
local run of this tier is a guaranteed 15-minute wait for nothing.

**2. A timeout reports as `0 tests` rather than as "unknown".**
`[TOTALS] simulation: 0 tests, 0 fail (FAIL)` reads like a measurement. It is
not one -- no test was observed to pass or fail. This is the repo's house
failure mode (silent wrongness) wearing a green-adjacent number: "0 fail" is
literally true and completely misleading.

## Probable cause of the slowness (partially diagnosed, not proven)

Running GUT directly against `res://tests/unit/simulation` floods stdout with one
line per RNG draw:

```
[VerificationTracker] RNG: event_hist_arxiv_218ce086ce67d573=0.948207 -> 69befb4da53334e3...
```

Sampled mid-run, the Godot process had **16.2 minutes wall clock against 7.9
seconds of user CPU** -- it is blocked on I/O, not computing. The print is
`debug_mode`-gated (`godot/autoload/verification_tracker.gd:225-226`), so it is
test-only and does **not** ship to players; a sim test turns it on deliberately.

Caveat, stated because it undercuts the theory: redirecting stdout to a file
instead of a pipe did **not** fix it. So console/pipe I/O is at most part of the
story and something else is also slow or stuck. Not chased further -- a release
was in flight.

## Asks

1. Add a `--timeout` flag to `run_godot_tests.py` so the tier can at least be
   run to completion locally.
2. Make a timeout report as **UNKNOWN / DID NOT RUN**, never as `0 tests, 0 fail`.
   A gate that cannot distinguish "nothing failed" from "nothing ran" is the
   exact defect #640 fixed for the fast gate; the slow tier still has it.
3. Find the real Windows slowness. Start by checking whether the per-RNG-draw
   debug print can be buffered or suppressed under GUT, then bisect the 8 files
   in `godot/tests/unit/simulation/` for the one that dominates.

## Consequence accepted for v0.14.0

v0.14.0 shipped with the simulation tier verified **only in CI**, not locally,
with that stated plainly in the handover rather than smoothed over. The fast gate
was green locally both before and after the change (1212 tests, 0 failures,
119/119 files -- identical counts).

issues.title: feat(art): a share set -- the missing route from "Pip likes it" to a public surface (126 candidates, 6.3% text-leak measured)
issues.body:
## The question

Pip, after applying 262 verdicts to the `an0807` art night: *"There are a shit
load of art assets I just judged, let's also figure out who owns me promoting
them up so we can social media / website them in the announcement run?"*

## Ownership -- verified, and it holds

- **Into the game:** ADR-0019. Generated -> Library -> Packed, and the only path
  into `godot/assets/` is a mechanically verified demand entry. pdoom1 owns it.
- **Onto a public surface:** `coordination#31` A2 bit 3, **`pdoom1-website` owns
  `publishable`**. Confirmed against both pdoom1's Phase 3 ballot ("pdoom1 does
  not want it and should not be given it. The website offered; take the offer")
  and the recorder's minute ("**SURVIVED.** Ruled. Pip: yes, build it"). Nothing
  here takes that gate back.

**One correction to the framing I was handed:** ADR-0019 does not use
`promotable/contested/held/blocked` -- those are `#1107`'s vocabulary. The ADR's
states are Generated / Library / Packed, plus "packed-but-undemanded" discovered
by measurement. It mentions publication, the website, and public surfaces **not
once**. That is not an oversight in the ADR; it is the gap.

## The gap, confirmed

ADR-0019 routes art that a **game slot** demands. An asset Pip likes that no slot
needs is never packed, so **there is nothing for the website to pull** -- it has
no route to a public surface at all. On this run that is *all 143 of his keeps*.
The website cannot exercise a gate over an empty set.

## What this adds

A **share set**: a tracked declaration of Library art pdoom1 offers for public
use, derived from verdicts already applied. Pip does not review anything twice.

| file | what |
|---|---|
| `docs/copy/ART_SHARE_SET.md` | the human doc -- read this first |
| `docs/copy/art_share_set.json` | the manifest the website pulls (143 entries) |
| `docs/copy/art_share_set_prompts.json` | `prompt_sha256` -> full prompt body |
| `tools/assets/build_share_set.py` | the generator (`--check`, `--html`, `--stage`) |
| `tools/art_review/scan_text_leak.py` | the OCR text gate |
| `tools/art_review/text_scan_art_night_2026-08-07.json` | its output, the evidence |

It lives in `docs/copy/` because that folder is the ACTIVE POLICY seam: the
website reads the game, never the reverse. `README.md` gains it as a seam entry,
so the website seat learns of it by reading the contract rather than by being
told. The website never touches `review_state.json`, which stays a pdoom1
internal.

## What qualifies, and the arguments

`keep` is **necessary, not sufficient**. `serve_review.py` defines it as "accept
it" -- taste, and only taste. ADR-0019 agrees from the other end: "Verdicts still
gate Library admission (taste)... none of them implies packing."

- **`iterate` excluded (56).** Not on a rule -- on his own words. Every note he
  left on an `iterate` in this run is a complaint (*"slightly too washed out,
  composition feels odd"*, *"this composition feels weird"*, *"slightyl too
  crisp"*), and every note he left on a `keep` is praise. `iterate` is defined as
  "on-brief but not final". Publishing one publishes an image he already called
  wrong.
- **`discard` excluded (63).**
- **Unjudged excluded (390 of 652)**, including all of `l1_grid` (220) and
  `l0_anchors` (54). Unjudged is not a quiet yes. Note `l1_grid` was described to
  me as a hero-shaped batch -- it is 1536x1024, but it carries **zero verdicts**,
  so it cannot enter.
- **Older Library assets excluded, structurally.** The builder cannot emit an
  entry without a run-ledger line and a `.meta.json` sidecar. An unattributable
  asset therefore *cannot* enter -- a mechanism, not a policy anyone must
  remember. `ASSET_PROVENANCE_SCOPE_2026-08-06` is why: 96.3% attributable by
  class, but 31.6% of packed assets have their only evidence in a gitignored
  single-copy directory and 6 are unattributable outright. That cannot back a
  public claim. Widening needs the `coordination#32` backfill first.

## Tiers -- because the consumer wants images to look at

143 entries, **126 publication candidates**:

| tier | n | |
|---|---:|---|
| `hero` | 5 | `keep` AND he typed praise -- *"love this"*, *"love this one"*, *"touch of green is nice"*, *"nice and warm"*, *"Nice altar, good stylishness"* |
| `feature` | 121 | `keep`, text-clean scene, no note either way |
| `reference` | 8 | `keep`, but colour swatch sheets. **Not candidates** -- labelled rather than dropped in front of the website seat unexplained |
| `quarantine_text` | 9 | `keep`, but OCR found lettering |

The `hero` rule leans on a measured property of *these 262 verdicts* -- notes on
keeps are praise, notes on iterates are reservations -- not a general law. The
note text ships in every entry so a reader can check that rather than take it.

## Text leak: measured, 6.3% of keeps

The run banned text in every prompt. It leaked.

RapidOCR (CPU, offline) over all 262 judged masters -- **17 carry a detection, 14
at confidence >= 0.60. Among the 143 keeps, 9. A 6.3% leak rate.**

Validated before trusting: fires on the known positive `s17_f01` ("DESICCANT",
conf 0.89), silent on two known-clean images.

The worst are not garbled, which is the point -- `'Plan A'` / `'Plan B'` /
`'Final Decision'` at 0.85 on a whiteboard, `'PENDING'` / `'APPROVED'` /
`'REJECTED'` at 0.83-0.88 on a status board. Some are garbled, which is worse in
public: `'PENDOVED'`, `'PPROVED'`, `'Nex+ Steps'`, `'De Bg aat'`.

**Ten of the seventeen are subject `s07`**, one recurring status-board scene. The
leak concentrates in prompts describing a surface a real room would letter -- so
the fix is that subject, not the pipeline.

**Any detection quarantines**, not just a confident one: a false quarantine costs
one image in 130, a false pass puts a garbled word on an image chosen precisely
for being prominent. Confidences travel with the entry so a borderline call can
be overruled on the evidence.

**Honest limit: this is a LOWER BOUND.** OCR misses small, low-contrast and
stylised lettering. A clean scan is evidence of absence, not proof of it. And
`s17_f01` -- the one leak found by eye -- is in the *unjudged* remainder, so
leakage is not confined to what he reviewed.

## Provenance, and the limit it cannot clear

Every entry carries `origin: generated_model`, model, backend, `run_id`,
`job_id`, `prompt_sha256`, UTC timestamp, quality, tariff cost. Full prompt
bodies ship **in git**, so "machine-generated, this model, this prompt" is
substantiable from a fresh clone rather than from a gitignored sidecar -- which
is exactly the weakness the provenance pass found in the older material.
Rebuilding that failure would have been the `coordination#15` shape.

**The API exposes no seed.** `seed: null` with a note in every entry. The record
establishes *what was asked for*, not how to reproduce the output. Public copy
should say "generated with this model from this prompt", never "reproducible".
Cost figures are tariff arithmetic (`cost_is_billed_truth: false`).

## Surfaces

Per entry, derived from pixel size rather than asserted. **Web and social: yes**,
at any normal display size. **Print at poster size: no, for every entry.** 1536px
long edge is ~5.1in at 300dpi and this pipeline has no upscale path. A poster
needs a regenerated source, not a resample.

## No bytes in git

The manifest carries paths. The 126 candidates are ~354MB, `ART_MASTERS_POLICY`
forbids art over 1MB in git, and the masters bucket is deliberately non-public
("NON-public (auth-only, not a web path)") -- so there is no surface the website
can fetch from today. Bridging that is a deliberate handover and Pip's call, not
something a build script should do quietly. `--stage DIR` prepares it off-git;
already run to `G:\tmp\pdoom1-art-masters\share_set_2026-08-07`.

## What this cannot offer, said plainly

Every candidate is an **L1** image: `medium` quality, one variant per cell, from
an unattended wide-net wave. **L2 and L3 are unrun** -- they need a picks file,
and ~USD 35 of the funded budget is unspent. L3 is the level whose entire purpose
is few, large, `high`-quality heroes.

So: 126 competent images Pip liked, fine for web and social, **none of them made
to be a hero**. The right answer to "the website wants beautiful things" is
generating better ones with the headroom that exists, not widening this set. That
is Pip's spend decision; this PR exists so he can make it knowing exactly what
the free alternative already contains.

## Two silent-wrongness bugs found while building this

1. A missing text scan made the builder emit an **ungated** manifest with 9 extra
   "candidates" and say nothing -- indistinguishable from a gated one. Now a hard
   error, with an explicit `--no-text-scan` that stamps the manifest as ungated.
2. Flat staging by basename **collided**: `l1_palette` and `l1_probe` both contain
   cell `s01_r01_p01`, from *different models* (gpt-image-1.5 vs gpt-image-2), and
   one silently overwrote the other. Staged names now carry the block, and
   uniqueness is asserted rather than assumed.

## The separate commit you should look at first

`chore(art-review)` commits `review_state.json`, which was **uncommitted in the
main checkout** -- 3,081 added verdicts including all 262 from this run, plus a
week of pixellab verdicts. It is the only copy, and this repo has lost in-flight
work to `git reset --hard` in the main checkout twice in 24 hours. Kept as its
own commit so it can be reverted independently.

**If your working copy of that file is dirty when you pull: KEEP YOURS** (it is
newer and a superset), then re-run `python tools/assets/build_share_set.py`.

## Open to disagreement

- `reference` (swatch sheets) could just be omitted rather than labelled. I kept
  them so the website seat is told what they are instead of inferring it.
- The `hero` rule is 5 assets resting on 5 notes. If Pip disagrees with any of
  them the tier is wrong by 20%.
- Quarantining on any detection will hold back some images whose "text" is
  texture. That is the deliberate trade; the evidence to overturn it is in the
  entry.

Open: `G:\Documents\Organising_Life\Code\pdoom1\art_generated\share_set.html`

Not wired into pre-commit: `build_share_set.py --check` needs `art_generated/`,
which is gitignored, so it cannot run in CI or on a fresh clone. Run it by hand
after touching verdicts.

Nothing was moved, deleted, or promoted into `godot/`.

issues.title: godot/data/historical_events.json carries two mojibake titles; the upstream repair cannot reach a hand-carried copy
issues.body:
**The shipped event snapshot carries two mojibake titles.**

Filed by the `pdoom-data` seat. Measured on `Bort` at 2026-08-07 17:0x AEST, twice: once by an independent scan, then again by hand before filing.

*(Rewritten 17:2x -- the first version of this body was mechanically derived from the sibling report filed as `pdoom1-website#282` and carried phrasing that belonged to that repo. This is the pdoom1-specific version.)*

## The finding

`godot/data/historical_events.json`, the 1,194-record snapshot taken from `pdoom-data`:

    uk_ai_safety_to_security_2025
      is        : 'UK AI Safety Institute \xe2†’ AI Security Institute'
      should be : 'UK AI Safety Institute -> AI Security Institute'

    us_aisi_to_caisi_2025
      is        : 'US AISI \xe2†’ Center for AI Standards and Innovation'
      should be : 'US AISI -> Center for AI Standards and Innovation'

`\xe2†’` is the bytes `E2 86 92` -- `U+2192` RIGHTWARDS ARROW in UTF-8 -- read as CP1252. Single-level mangling; the recovered strings contain nothing further suspicious.

Whether a player sees these depends on whether either event surfaces in play, which is a pdoom1 question rather than a pdoom-data one.

## Use `->`, not the recovered arrow

Upstream `pdoom-data` repaired these on 2026-08-06 to the ASCII `->`, because that repo is ASCII-only and its repair rule is an explicit substitution map that errors on unmapped characters rather than guessing. Writing back the reconstructed `U+2192` would leave the copies disagreeing in a **new** way rather than the old one. Verified upstream on `main`:

    'UK AI Safety Institute -> AI Security Institute'

## Why the upstream fix did not reach you

`pdoom-data` shipped a transcoding gate today (`pdoom-data#69`). It scans every JSON and JSONL under its own `data/` tree, and **it cannot see this file by construction** -- `godot/data/historical_events.json` is a frozen hand-carried copy that does not regenerate, which is exactly why the 08-06 repair did not propagate.

So the gate protects the source and not the consumer. This seat has no standing to choose pdoom1's answer, but the two available shapes are: the snapshot becomes a **refreshed artifact** with a recorded provenance and a re-sync step, or pdoom1 runs its **own** transcoding check over `godot/data/` in CI. They are not exclusive, and only the first stops it recurring.

Detection rule if you want it standalone -- and deliberately reimplement rather than import, so that a defect in one implementation is not invisible to both:

> a string is corrupt if it contains `U+00C2`, `U+00C3` or `U+00E2` **and** `s.encode('cp1252').decode('utf-8')` succeeds and differs. The result is what it should have been.

Two traps, both of which cost this seat time today: split JSONL on `\n` only, because `str.splitlines()` also breaks on `U+2028` and `U+0085`, which occur inside string values in these corpora and will fragment records into false findings; and print findings `ascii()`-escaped, because a Windows console re-mangles mojibake on output and a genuinely corrupt string can print back looking correct.

## Scope, measured rather than assumed

A cross-repo sweep today scanned 536 files in `pdoom1` (`godot/data/` and `docs/`), 347 in `pdoom1-website`, and 68 markdown files in `coordination`. **Every file on disk decoded cleanly as UTF-8**; the corruption is inside string values, not in file encoding. Findings were exactly these two records, in this file and in `pdoom1-website/public/data/events.json` (filed as `pdoom1-website#282`). `pdoom1/docs/` is clean. `coordination` is clean.
